text.text_excerpt: Such an adorable thrift store! And for such a great cause! I stumbled upon this store on a walk down Magazine Street, and was ecstatic to find out (on that particular day) that everything was marked half off the tag price! I'm already a sucker for a bargain on clothes, but this hooked me. A thrift store is only as good as the donations, and luckily, this store (located near the Garden District) does not disappoint! In addition, a portion of the money gets donated to a local animal shelter (or a few different ones... Not sure, but either way I'm glad some portion gets donated). Last but not least, the cherry on top is the staff! I've been a few times since my first visit, and they're alway...

This is a great thrift store with excellent pricing, unlike the Buffalo Exchange across the street. I've found better clothes at No Fleas for cheaper prices than what I would've paid for at BE. My greatest finds at No Fleas (so far): *A pair of acid wash Seven7 skinny jeans that would regularly cost $100 only cost me $12 at No Fleas. Brand new, no stains, no rips! *A Land's End tweed pencil skirt, mint condition $8. *Amazing Bloomingdale's bandana $3.50 *Mary Engelbreit enamel pin $2.50 All amazing things that would've cost double the price at BE. I hate to disparage one store while praising another, but it's so easy to compare the two since they happen to be located right across the stre...

New Orleans is NOT known for their thrift stores, let me tell ya!! That being said, I am VERY happy that I discovered No Fleas Market. The staff are friendly, the clothes are in great shape, and I always walk out with a new wardrobe. Today my bf and I were there and one of the sales associates showed him a sweater he might like. It was a great quirky sweater that matches his style perfectly. As we were checking out, another associate pointed out that this brand, Coogi, has sweaters in the Smithsonian and its worth some major $$$ all for just $10! +++ the proceeds go to some wonderful nonprofits for animals.
